licence: CC BY-NC-SA 4.0 (LICENSE.md in abc-data); the site states free, registration-free use for individual non-commercial research
how_found: The assigned URL redirects to abacus.acdh.oeaw.ac.at; footer links the GitHub org, and the site's "Zitieren/Kontakt" page names https://github.com/Austrian-Baroque-Corpus/abc-data as the TEI/XML data repository. Repo README: "This repository contains the TEI/XML data for the ABaC:us project."
note: https://acdh.oeaw.ac.at/abacus/ 301s to https://abacus.acdh.oeaw.ac.at/ (200). Edition itself has no DOI; the only DOI on the citation page is for a 2016 ZfdG article (10.17175/2016_005). Sibling repos in the same org: abc-app (MIT), abc-register. Could not confirm a schema/ODD folder: GitHub API rate limit hit and the web tree view is JS-only.

how_found: Site footer and about.html link only the app repo acdh-oeaw/akademie-static; the data repo was found by GitHub search restricted to org:acdh-oeaw ("akademie-data — data repo for Akademieprotokolle"), README confirms it, contains data/ and a dump/ of the legacy app.
note: Site banner says it is currently being technically reworked ("Die Website wird derzeit technisch überarbeitet"). No LICENSE file in akademie-data and no licence statement on the site, so reuse terms are undeclared. About page confirms transcriptions were converted to TEI XML. Data repo last updated 2026-07-31, so actively maintained.

edition_name: Alexander von Humboldt: Sämtliche Schriften digital
how_found: Not on the /text landing page; found on the project documentation page https://humboldt.unibe.ch/erschliessung/dokumentation, which links the repo. Repo README confirms: TEI P5 XML, project site humboldt.unibe.ch, licence CC BY-SA 4.0.
note: Watch the contradiction: the reading interface carries a boilerplate copyright notice forbidding download and reproduction, while the documentation page and the GitHub repo release the texts under CC BY-SA 4.0. Encoding follows TEI P5 as applied by the Deutsches Textarchiv (DTABf customization) plus a project character inventory (/meta/characters, /meta/combinings); no standalone ODD file is published. The site also offers a full-corpus download button and per-text XML/TXT export from the viewer toolbar.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (transcriptions, TEI encoding, editorial content and translations; digital facsimiles follow the holding institutions' terms)
how_found: The Nutzungsbedingungen page states the TEI XML transcription and edition data are on heiDATA and links doi.org/10.11588/data/FNKJ2Y; the DOI resolves to the heiDATA (Dataverse) dataset. Its file listing (via the Dataverse API) holds a single file, DAH_Edition_TEI.xml, text/xml, about 2.0 MB.
note: Edition version 2.0, Heidelberg 2026. The whole edition is one XML file, not a per-witness corpus. Encoding is governed by the project TEI-Handbuch (https://digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/hvad/materialien/teihandbuch.html), which states it depends on the heiEditions validation schema and documentation and the heiEDITIONS Concepts ontology, so a customization exists but is not exposed as an ODD file. Caution: digi.ub.uni-heidelberg.de/diglit/* is behind an Anubis anti-bot gate; the /ahd/ static pages are fetchable normally.

edition_name: Arnold Schönberg: Briefwechsel mit den Verlagen C. F. Peters und C. F. Peters Corporation
how_found: Site root serves a meta-refresh to /cfp/index.html but is behind a Cloudflare managed challenge (403 to any non-browser client), so the in-site pages could not be inspected. Searched GitHub for orgs/repos (Schoenberg-Peters, Schoenberg-CFP, schoenberg+peters) and Zenodo for the edition title: nothing.
note: No public source repository or deposit found for this edition. Its sibling project states the Peters edition follows the same XML structure and guidelines as the Universal-Edition/Dreililien edition (www.schoenberg-ue.at/editionsrichtlinien), whose data and ODDs are public at https://github.com/Schoenberg-UE/Schoenberg-Data, but the Peters letters do not appear in that repo (its README scopes it explicitly to the UE/Dreililien edition). Any download offered inside the web app could not be verified because of the bot challenge; a human browser would be needed.

edition_name: Arnold Schönberg: Briefwechsel mit den Verlagen Universal-Edition und Dreililien
how_found: Site itself unreachable to automated clients (Cloudflare managed challenge, 403). Found via GitHub search for "Schönberg": the org Schoenberg-UE holds Schoenberg-Data, whose README opens "Das Repo Schoenberg-Data bildet die Datenveröffentlichung der Edition Arnold Schönberg: Briefwechsel mit den Verlagen Universal-Edition und Dreililien (https://www.schoenberg-ue.at)".
note: Best-documented repo in this batch. data/letters and data/documents hold the TEI letters and documents by year, data/indices the registers, plus Versionen.xml with release history. schema/ contains ediarum.asue.odd (letters and documents), ediarum.asue.register.odd, ediarum.asue.api.odd (the form offered for download in the web app, with keys resolved to absolute URLs), datatypes.odd.xml and mei-source.xml, generated by ODD chaining from ediarum.BASE.data-model and ediarum.REGISTER.data-model, with compiled ODD and RelaxNG in schema/compiledODD and schema/out. guidelines/ holds the Editionsrichtlinien in XML and HTML. No LICENSE file and no licence statement in the README, so reuse terms are undeclared. Web app is separate: https://github.com/Schoenberg-UE/Schoenberg-WebApp (eXist-db). Hybrid edition, the XML also feeds the print volume (print-workflow/).

edition_name: Arthur Schnitzler – Briefwechsel mit Autorinnen und Autoren
doi: 10.5281/zenodo.20309129 (concept DOI, always resolves to the latest version)
how_found: Linked directly from the edition site ("Offene Daten auf GitHub"); CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json in the repo confirm title, licence and concept DOI.
note: CITATION.cff notes the facsimiles are excluded for legal reasons; only transcriptions and indices are in the repo. Encoding documentation at https://schnitzler-briefe.acdh.oeaw.ac.at/elemente.html states that data/meta holds schnitzler-briefe-schema.xsd and schnitzler-briefe-schematron.sch, so a customization is documented but as XSD plus Schematron, not as an ODD. Also long-term archived in ARCHE (hdl.handle.net/21.11115/0000-000E-7538-0). Funding for 2025-2029: FWF 10.55776/PAT1998524.

edition_name: Arthur Schnitzler – Chronik. Eine digitale Ressource zu den einzelnen Tagen seines Lebens
how_found: Linked from the edition site alongside the static-site repo; .zenodo.json and CITATION.cff in the repo confirm scope and licence, and the Zenodo record was found by title search.
note: Strictly a TEI listEvent aggregation, one entry per day of Schnitzler's adult life, pulling together events, readings, letters, diary entries and cultural appointments, rather than a text edition, which matters if the corpus counts edited documents. The site states each day is also retrievable as XML or JSON by appending the date (example given: 1927-11-07.xml); I did not verify an individual day URL. No LICENSE file in the repo despite the CITATION.cff declaration. Repo is large (about 1.1 GB reported size).

edition_name: Arthur Schnitzler: Lektüren. Digitale Edition der Leseliste von Arthur Schnitzler
licence: declared inconsistently: CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json say CC BY-SA 4.0, but the repo's LICENSE file is CC BY 4.0
how_found: Linked from the edition site; CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json in the repo confirm title and licence, Zenodo record found by title search.
note: Single repo holding both TEI data (data/) and the generated static site (html/), unlike the sibling projects which split data and app. Licence discrepancy above is worth flagging to whoever reuses the data. A PDF of the 2013 print edition is also served from the site.

licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (GitHub licence metadata and CITATION.cff)
how_found: Site links it under "Zum Projekt" as "Offene Daten auf gitHub"; repo default branch is master and carries CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json confirming "Arthur Schnitzler: Tagebuch 1879-1931. Digitale Edition – Quelldaten".
note: No current DOI stated in CITATION.cff. An older Zenodo deposit exists from when the repo lived under acdh-oeaw: 10.5281/zenodo.3527718 (concept) / 10.5281/zenodo.3527719 (v1.0, licence "other-open"); it predates the move to the arthur-schnitzler org and should not be cited as the current edition DOI. Note the default branch is master, not main. Data is a retro-digitization of the 1981-2000 ÖAW print edition.

edition_name: Auden Musulin Papers: A Digital Edition of W. H. Auden's Letters to Stella Musulin
licence: CC BY 4.0 (amp-data); the web app is MIT
how_found: Site links the app repo and two Zenodo DOIs (app and data); the data DOI 10.5281/zenodo.13149400 resolves to "Auden-Musulin-Papers/amp-data: v1.0.0", which identifies the canonical repo. Repo README confirms data/editions holds the XML/TEI-encoded edition files.
note: Prefer the GitHub repo over the Zenodo zip: the Zenodo record is a frozen v1.0.0 snapshot (Aug 2024) while the repo was updated in Dec 2025. The editorial declaration documents TEI P5 practice in detail (minimal intervention, entities via <rs>) but names no ODD or schema file; the repo does have a framework/ directory whose contents I could not enumerate (GitHub API rate limit). Also archived in ARCHE at https://id.acdh.oeaw.ac.at/auden-musulin-papers.
